supports:
Doubling bus frequency on every major corridor
The city paying for transit expansion
quote: We will double bus frequency on every major corridor, and the city will pay for it.
source: Mayoral Debate, League of Voters Forum
real_world_impact: Expect more frequent buses and new routes, funded partly by a proposed 0.25% sales tax increase. Commuters without cars gain the most, while everyone pays slightly more at the register.

supports: Riders and private partners covering transit costs
quote: Riders and private partners should carry transit costs, not every taxpayer in the city.
real_world_impact: Local taxes would likely stay flat, but bus fares could rise and low-ridership routes may be cut. Service would depend more on private contractors and ridership revenue.

supports:
A housing bond for income-restricted homes
Allowing taller buildings near transit stations
quote: I support a housing bond, paired with zoning reform near transit stations.
real_world_impact: A voter-approved bond would add a small amount to property tax bills to fund income-restricted units. Some neighborhoods near transit would see taller buildings permitted.

supports: Faster permits so private builders add housing
quote: Cut the permit backlog and let builders build. Supply is the answer, not subsidies.
real_world_impact: Permits would move faster and fees could drop, which may increase new market-rate housing. There would be little direct city spending on income-restricted units.

supports: City-funded legal aid to help immigrant families stay together
opposes: Local police holding people for ICE without a judge's warrant
quote: Our police should focus on local safety. I'd fund a legal-aid office for immigrant families.
real_world_impact: The city budget would include roughly $1.2M a year for legal aid and outreach. Local police would limit honoring federal detainer requests without a judicial warrant.

supports: Local police cooperating with ICE detainer requests under federal law
opposes: Spending city money on immigrant legal services
quote: The city should follow federal law and not spend local dollars on federal responsibilities.
source: Mayoral Debate, League of Voters Forum
real_world_impact: No new city spending on immigrant legal services would be added to the budget. Local police would continue to honor federal detainer requests under existing practice.

supports:
Keeping police patrol staffing at current levels
Mental-health responders for non-violent 911 calls
quote: Keep patrol staffing level and add mental-health responders for non-violent calls.
real_world_impact: A new crisis-response team would take some 911 calls currently handled by officers. This adds about $800K to the city budget without cutting patrol positions.

opposes: New programs before response times improve
quote: Response times come first. Fund two more fire crews before any new programs.
real_world_impact: Fire and EMS response times in District 1 would likely improve. Funding would be shifted from other discretionary programs instead of raising taxes.

supports: Better dispatch technology to stretch the current budget
quote: We can get more from the budget we have through better dispatch technology.
real_world_impact: Overall public safety spending would stay roughly flat. Improvements would come from software and process changes rather than new staff.

supports: A citywide stormwater fee on utility bills
quote: Flooding is a citywide problem and should be paid for citywide.
real_world_impact: A new stormwater fee of about $6 a month would appear on utility bills. Flood-prone streets would be prioritized for drainage upgrades within five years.

supports: Fixing the ten worst-flooding blocks with existing funds
opposes: A new stormwater fee for now
quote: Fix the worst ten blocks now with existing capital funds, then reassess.
real_world_impact: No new fee in the short term, with targeted repairs funded from the current capital budget. Other planned capital projects could be delayed to cover it.

supports: A dedicated stormwater utility, funded by a fee and a bond
quote: I've designed these systems. We need a full stormwater utility, bonded and built in one go.
real_world_impact: A dedicated stormwater utility would be created with a monthly fee and a bond issue. Construction would be faster and broader, with higher upfront cost to households and businesses.

supports:
Grants for vacant storefronts that hire locally
Paying for them from the existing economic development fund
quote: Targeted grants for storefronts that hire locally, funded by the existing economic development fund.
real_world_impact: Some vacant storefronts would receive startup grants tied to local hiring. Business taxes would stay at current levels.

supports: Dropping the business license fee for businesses under ten employees
quote: Eliminate the business license fee for anyone under ten employees. That's the incentive.
real_world_impact: Small businesses would save a few hundred dollars a year in fees. The city would lose that revenue, which may require trims elsewhere in the general fund.

supports:
Putting a school levy on the ballot
Raising teacher pay to keep teachers from leaving
quote: We are losing teachers to neighboring districts. I'll put a levy on the ballot.
real_world_impact: Homeowners could see about $120 a year added to property taxes if voters approve the levy. Teacher salaries would rise and average class sizes would drop by an estimated two students.

supports: An independent audit of district central-office spending
opposes: A new school tax before that audit
quote: Before asking taxpayers for more, we need an independent audit of central-office spending.
real_world_impact: No new school tax would be proposed in the near term. Any raises for teachers would depend on savings found through the audit.
